item.title: Google DeepMind researchers argue AI development is on pace to move beyond human-level AGI to ASI, which consistently outperforms groups of human experts (Tim Genewein/DeepMind Institute)
item.description: For decades, AI research has been focused on a monumental milestone: building artificial general intelligence, or AGI - machines that match humans across nearly all cognitive tasks. It was always clear that, in principle, intelligence could progress beyond human level, but the prospect of AGI was far enough off, and surrounded by ample uncertainties of its own, that looking past it felt premature. item.title: Source: Iconiq invested more than $6B in Anthropic; its estimated 1.8% stake was worth ~$31.8B at Thursday's close, a 430%+ return on investment (Richard Nieva/Forbes)
item.description: Iconiq Capital has made a significant strategic investment exceeding $6 billion in AI startup Anthropic, with its roughly 1.8% equity stake now valued at approximately $31.8 billion. This surge occurs as Anthropic prepares for a landmark IPO, highlighting the massive capital deployment and high-leverage competition within the foundational model and AI ecosystem.

item.title: Anthropic’s US$1.5 trillion debut rewrites venture capital’s playbook
item.description: AI lab Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq on November 19 at an $83 IPO price, closing at $97.17 with a fully diluted valuation of $1.8 trillion. This liquidity event yields massive returns for early backers like Menlo Ventures and Spark Capital, signaling a structural shift in AI venture capital toward large-scale SPV-driven funding models.

item.title: Sources: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion LLM developer Inception for $500M+ plus earnouts; talks began before Jensen Huang's resignation (The Information)
item.description: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion-based LLM developer Inception for over $500 million, including earnouts. Inception recently launched Mercury 3, a model utilizing diffusion scaling laws to outperform autoregressive models like GPT-6.1-Sol in specific benchmarks, achieving speeds exceeding 1,000 tokens per second.

item.title: Sources: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving now to let the White House get a successor confirmed before Democrats take the Senate in January (Axios)
item.description: US National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is stepping down to provide a transition window for his successor to be confirmed by the Senate before Democrats gain control in January. As the head of the Office of the National Cyber Director, Cairncross led federal cybersecurity strategy and notably directed technical reviews of AI firms like Anthropic following commerce-led export control implementations.

item.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
item.description: Apple is pivoting its AI strategy by recruiting for a 'Proactive, Agentic AI' engineering lead to develop autonomous systems capable of cross-app interaction, code debugging, and complex task planning. The initiative, integrating teams from Siri, UI Frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models, aims to move beyond static voice commands toward an autonomous agent environment capable of multi-step execution across devices.

item.title: Apple Is Working on AI Agent for Device Control, Apps, Browsing and Coding
item.description: Bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of users. Here are the details. ### Apple working on AI agent that can code, browse the web, more In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that new job listings on Apple’s website indicate the company’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf. item.title: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
item.description: Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang resigned following misconduct allegations, causing the stock to drop nearly 40% from its October 6th peak, despite a record-breaking Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion and the rapid shipment of the Vera Rubin platform. Chairman Harvey Jones has confirmed that the board will not reinstate Huang and has initiated an executive search to stabilize leadership.

item.title: What’s With All These Outages?
item.description: Major infrastructure outages occurred sequentially at Microsoft, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, the NSA, and Apple. Despite official denials of cyberattacks, market anxiety is mounting due to the convergence of these failures with Anthropic's reported $1.5 trillion IPO plans, the first Nvidia earnings report post-Jensen Huang's resignation, and new US executive orders aimed at restricting Chinese entities from accessing AI compute via cloud rentals.

item.title: Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
item.description: Intuit has reached an agreement to sell its email-marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock, slated for closure in early 2027. This divestiture, representing a loss of over 70% from the $12 billion acquisition price in 2021, follows Mailchimp's stagnant revenue growth and its role as a drag on Intuit's broader financial valuation.

item.title: At a Senate hearing, Trump's CISA director nominee Michael LoSapio dodged questions about the agency's priorities, denied January 6 was an attack, and more (Eric Geller/Cybersecurity Dive)
item.description: Michael LoSapio, CISO of Palantir and Trump’s nominee for CISA director, faced significant scrutiny during his Senate Homeland Security Committee confirmation hearing. He evaded questions regarding the administration’s budget cuts to CISA and denied the nature of the January 6, 2021 Capitol attack, raising alarms among lawmakers about his political alignment and commitment to agency autonomy.

item.title: The Jensen Huang Blast Radius Has Hit His Favorite Restaurants
item.description: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following allegations of multiple extramarital affairs. The incident has triggered widespread public scrutiny, with small businesses in Taipei weighing the reputational impact of their past association with him against the marketing value of his high-profile visits.

item.title: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
item.description: Igor D’iu, a 25-year-old Russian national, has been indicted for espionage after illegally entering the U.S. to surveil employees of a Silicon Valley defense tech firm, widely identified as Palantir. The defendant allegedly gathered intelligence on the company's military support and weapon supply chain to Ukraine.

item.title: Meta’s Muse Charm might cost $300
item.description: Meta plans to launch the Muse Charm, a wearable device featuring real-time voice and avatar interaction, at a $300 price point by this December. The device integrates a fingerprint sensor for instant AI agent access without smartphone intervention and includes a 12-month complimentary 5G data plan from Verizon, while Meta has deferred its internal smartwatch project until 2027.

item.title: Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage
item.description: Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches. In a post on X, Google’s vice president of product, Robby Stein, shows how you can now open a collapsible sidebar to view and continue your AI chats. Based on the GIF shared by Stein, it looks like you can open the sidebar by clicking the gray bar that appears on the left side of your screen. From there, Google will show a list of the searches you’ve made using AI Mode, along with the ability to start a new thread, search your threads, or

item.title: Source: Meta plans to charge $300 for its forthcoming Muse Charm device and include a free 5G data plan from Verizon for up to 12 months (Jyoti Mann/The Information)
item.description: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled the Muse Charm, a $300 handheld AI device bundled with a 12-month free 5G plan from Verizon, at Meta Connect. The device replaces traditional UI with a customizable, 'fuzzy' mascot avatar to handle tasks like email management, scheduling, and purchases, aiming to shift consumer perception through anthropomorphic interaction.

item.title: AI industry growth remains strong, but the pace is slowing
item.description: Ramp AI Index and OpenRouter data indicate that US corporate AI usage is hitting record highs while the average cost per million tokens has dropped below $0.45 due to aggressive pricing competition. Anthropic has surpassed OpenAI in both spending and volume market share, signaling a paradigm shift in the AI infrastructure market from a high-premium phase to a defensive pricing cycle.

item.title: A bipartisan group of 24+ House lawmakers forms the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, seeking to balance mitigating AI risks with maintaining US leadership in AI (Owen Dahlkamp/Politico)
item.description: Over 24 bipartisan House lawmakers, led by Representatives George Whitesides, Don Beyer, and Nathaniel Moran, have formed the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus. The group aims to serve as an active legislative conduit, bridging the gap between long-term policy formulation and rapid-response requirements by leveraging cross-sector intelligence to address AI-related incidents and security breaches.

item.title: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
item.description: Google has introduced 'Computer Use' capabilities to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, enabling the AI agent to navigate native apps, manage local files, and browse the web on the user's behalf. This feature is gated behind Gemini Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscriptions and is currently limited to English users in the U.S., requiring explicit user approval for agentic actions via a live preview interface.

item.title: Former Alibaba exec’s Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories
item.description: Everful, a cross-border supply chain platform co-founded by former Alibaba executive Sisi Song and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, raised $48.5 million in Series A funding led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India. The company leverages an AI-enabled platform to connect over 30,000 factories with small retailers, providing end-to-end services including sourcing, quality control, and logistics, achieving an annualized revenue of $100 million.

item.title: Gemini on Mac can now use your computer
item.description: Google has introduced the "Computer Use" feature to its Gemini app for macOS, enabling the AI to execute multi-step tasks across local files, desktop applications, and the web. Currently rolling out in the US, the feature allows users to designate app access while monitoring AI actions through a real-time background preview window.

item.title: Ubisoft Logs Strong Bookings as Players Welcome Assassin’s Creed Remake
item.description: Ubisoft Singapore's 'Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced' achieved 3.5 million sales within two weeks, accompanied by recent New Game+ and difficulty updates. Jean Guesdon, Head of AC Content, confirmed in the Fall 2026 Update that no further remakes are in development, with resources redirected to 'Codename Invictus' and the mainline 'Codename Hexe'.

item.title: Alphabet to Raise at Least $3.5 Billion With Canadian Debt Sale
item.description: Alphabet Inc. is planning to raise at least CA$5 billion through a five-part bond sale in the Canadian market, marking its return just six months after its inaugural CA$8.5 billion offering in May. The move is designed to leverage regional liquidity to optimize the company's global treasury and capital structure.

item.title: London-based Boltz, which is developing AI models to speed up drug discovery, raised a $110M Series A led by Bessemer, after raising a $28M seed in 2025 (John Reynolds/Tech.eu)
item.description: Boltz, an AI drug discovery startup spun out of MIT and now based in London, has raised $110 million in Series A funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners. The capital injection follows a $28 million seed round in 2025 and will be utilized to accelerate the development of its AI models for accelerated pharmaceutical research.

item.title: Chinese tech firms face a double hit as chip shipments stop and overseas cloud access disappears
item.description: The U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has tightened export controls by requiring licenses for AI compute access in third-party countries, effectively closing cloud loopholes. Simultaneously, TSMC and Samsung have halted shipments of advanced processors to certain Chinese clients pending license approval, forcing firms like Moonshot AI to cancel major compute contracts and triggering widespread supply chain disruption.

item.title: Google Built a Giant ‘Mirror Dimension’ Internet to Test Its Chrome AI Agents
item.description: Google's Chrome AI team has developed a controlled, expansive simulation environment dubbed the 'Mirror Dimension.' This sandbox hosts realistic versions of social media, e-commerce, and banking platforms, allowing researchers to evaluate the resilience of Gemini-powered web-browsing agents against prompt-injection attacks and other real-world vulnerabilities without risking the open web.

item.title: Anthropic's historic debut to put AI's promise and peril to Wall St test
item.description: Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic's record $81 billion IPO brings to Wall Street an avatar of a sector that proponents herald as an economic panacea, while detractors warn it has stoked a market bubble and could ultimately threaten humanity itself. More immediately, the Claude chatbot maker's debut after securing a $1.5 trillion valuation in the IPO, together with Tuesday's earnings report by AI poster child Nvidia, signals the industry has nominally passed the two big tests facing it this week. The listing comes nearly a month after Anthropic revealed its plans to go public. item.title: AMD Slides After Hunterbrook Shorts Stock, Cites Circular Deals
item.description: Short-selling firm Hunterbrook alleged that AMD continued providing BIOS firmware updates to IEIT Systems, a Chinese server manufacturer blacklisted by the U.S. in March 2025. While the report stopped short of proving a legal violation, the allegation triggered market concerns over AMD's supply chain traceability and compliance efficacy, causing an 8% drop in its share price.
